breaking.member: AbilityBar parts (cell, well, icon, figure, badge, label, sweep)
breaking.change: AbilityBar is now a strip of AbilitySlot components instead of drawing its own slots, so a slot looks the same alone and in a bar. Its only part is AbilityBar.frame; each slot's parts are AbilitySlot's. Its slots are 56 px at 100% text, shrink alike in a narrower place down to 44 px, and under that break into lines instead of overflowing (--ability-bar-slot-size, --ability-bar-slot-min).
breaking.fix: In a style pack or a game's CSS, style the slots through the AbilitySlot parts of the same names (AbilitySlot.cell, AbilitySlot.well, AbilitySlot.icon, AbilitySlot.figure, AbilitySlot.badge, AbilitySlot.label, AbilitySlot.sweep).

breaking.change: The orb is redrawn as a glass vessel in a metal bezel (a dark well in its liquid's hue, a waved surface, the sphere's shade and a gleam), round by default in every style and the same in both schemes, 112 px at 100% text. It no longer wears the well role, so OrbMeter.well is gone.
breaking.fix: Set the orb layer by layer through its tokens: the bezel (--orb-meter-rim, -rim-fill, -rim-width, -rim-shadow, -radius, -corner-shape, and -ornament for an image over it), the socket (-socket-fill, -socket-width), the glass (-well, -light, -glass-shadow, -gleam, -shade, -depth), the liquid (-health, -mana, -swell, -surface-width) and the value (-figure-size, -figure-ink, -figure-shadow); --orb-meter-size is its side.

added.summary: A new layout primitive for one line of like blocks (ability slots, party frames, quick items). Its data-fit children are each --layout-strip-item wide, so the strip is as wide as what it holds; where it is given less room they shrink alike, down to --layout-strip-item-min. With data-wraps and its count in --layout-strip-count it breaks into lines instead of going under that minimum.
A slot fills the place it is given: --ability-slot-size is its side (100% inside a strip), and its icon, lock and ring scale with it. It takes count, a quick item's number left.
Each threshold's star sits on the track where it falls, and the stars are the style's rating stars (--star-*): a lit star is gold with a glow, an unlit one a faint outline in a dark seat.
